title: Why odd numbers add up to squares
insight: Each odd number is exactly the L-shaped strip that grows an n by n square into an (n+1) by (n+1) square.

lines.text: Add up the first few odd numbers.
Every total is a perfect square. But why?
Draw each odd number as dots. Start with one.
Three dots bend around it, into an L.
Each odd number is exactly the L that grows the square by one.
So the first n odd numbers always fill an n by n square.
